key_insight: Self-supervised MRI foundation models work best when the pretraining objective matches the downstream task’s signal structure, with spectral MAE giving the strongest overall disease-detection gains.
clinical_relevance: This suggests future brain MRI AI models may improve disease detection if pretraining is tailored to fine anatomical detail or distributed feature patterns, rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach.
method: Compared Masked Autoencoders (MAE) with Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) for 3D brain MRI pretraining.
Added a spectral-domain reconstruction loss to MAE to better capture high-frequency anatomical detail.
Added variance-covariance regularization to JEPA to encourage less redundant latent features.
evidence_signal: The models were pretrained on heterogeneous single-contrast MRI volumes in a contrast-agnostic setting and evaluated across five downstream disease detection tasks.
watch_item: The reported gains may depend on how closely a downstream task matches the inductive bias of the chosen self-supervised objective, so results may not transfer equally to all MRI detection problems.
paper_title: Masked and Predictive Self-Supervised Foundation Models for 3D Brain MRI
